title: Week 8 Preview: Rematch Week, and the Model Likes Kai to Topple the Hulk
dek: Every matchup is a Week 1 rematch, the two 5-2 teams meet in a 51-49 coin flip, and the 6-1 juggernaut walks in as an underdog to a 2-5 team.
body: Welcome to Rematch Week. Every game on the Week 8 slate is a replay of Week 1, and the headliner is the closest game of the season so far. Team Pillbert and The Horse is Hea are both 5-2, and the model has Philly at 49% at home, which is the analytics version of a shrug. Sonny took the Week 1 meeting 106.42 to 102.1 and leads the all-time series 6-5. The stakes are clean: the winner climbs to 96 or 97 percent playoff odds, and the loser slides into the mid-80s.

The swing players are obvious. If Jahmyr Gibbs hits 32 or more, Alan's win chance jumps to 73%, and if Gibbs is held under 10, it craters to 28%. On the other side, a 25-point day from Jaxon Smith-Njigba pushes Sonny to 69%, while a quiet one under 8 drops him to 35%. This is also Sonny's first big test with Ashton Jeanty and Christian Watson after last week's deal with Mekhi, and he brings the better scoring résumé (853.6 to 817.8) into a game that will likely come down to a handful of plays.

Now the strangest number on the board: No Banner only HULK is 6-1, has won three straight, leads the league with 927.4 points, and is an underdog. The model makes Dawgs a 54% favorite on the road, even though Brucie won the Week 1 meeting 177.86 to 98.36 and leads the series 6-3. Ja'Marr Chase is the reason to believe: 27 or more and Kai's chances rise to 75%, while Josh Allen at 32-plus gives Ramon a 65% shot and Allen under 15 sinks him to 27%. Ramon is playing with house money at 100% with a win and 97% with a loss, but for Mekhi at 2-5, the gap between 26% and 11% is the whole season.

The real swing game is Habibsters vs. Ghostu-Spider SZN, a pair of 3-4 teams trying to stay above the cut line. Habib is a 72% home favorite on a two-game streak and has outscored Zoe by 137 points this season, but Z² already won this matchup 129.56 to 108.6 in Week 1. A win pushes Kaushal to 58% playoff odds, and a loss drops him to 23%; Zoe's range is 40% to 12%. Puka Nacua is the heavy lever (27-plus makes it 87%), though even a Puka dud leaves Habibsters at 56%. Zoe counters with a Jordan Love and Tucker Kraft stack, the most Wisconsin lineup decision possible, and she'll need it, because a 20-point Tetairoa McMillan game only gets her to 45%.

Finally, The fumblers try to snap a four-game skid against Counting or not Counting GV, and the model is giving Randy a 68% chance to do it. Week 1 was a 146.16 to 75.96 rout, and Derrick Henry at 26-plus makes Randy an 88% favorite. He's also rolling out a Caleb Williams and Colston Loveland stack, and a win moves him to 38% playoff odds versus 19% with a loss. JMoney is 1-6 and hanging by a 2% thread, so he needs Joe Burrow to throw for 29-plus fantasy points just to make it a coin flip. Under 16, it's 18%.

social.author: Sal Benedetto
social.text: Week 8 picks are UP and I've got FOUR locks. Habibsters is the lock of the week. Horse, HULK, and yes, Counting or not Counting GV. I don't ride four-game losing streaks. Never have. Write it down.

social.author: Fumbleheads Anonymous
social.text: Sal Benedetto said he doesn't ride four-game losing streaks and took a 1-6 team as a LOCK over us. Respectfully, sir, what.

social.author: Gamma Ray Gary
social.text: Nina Kessler: 'Records don't play this week's games; lineups do.' Cool. Our lineup is 6-1 with 927 points. Enjoy your lean on Dawgs, doc.

social.author: Web Slinger Wendy
social.text: Marcus Pell picking Ghostu-Spider SZN because 'rookies don't read the odds' is the only analysis I need this week. Love to Kraft, let's go.

social.author: Habib Hive
social.text: Marcus Pell saw a 72% favorite and two-time champ and said 'nah.' Contrarian for the clicks. Nina and Sal get it.

social.author: Dawg Pound Dre
social.text: Dana AND Nina both on Dawgs. 2-5 and the smart money still knows. Can't sleep, too hyped. Chase 27+ or bust.

social.author: Ghostu-Spider SZN
social.text: Matchday weekend. Jordan Love and Tucker Kraft, together in the lineup. We took this one 129.56 to 108.6 in Week 1. Let's run it back.

picks.game: Team Pillbert (Alan) vs The Horse is Hea (Sonny)

panel.take: This is Sonny's first big test with Ashton Jeanty and Christian Watson after the deal with Mekhi, and that depth matters in a game the model calls 51-49. I'm leaning Horse, but quietly.

Sonny took Week 1 by four points and leads the all-time series by a single game; history is begging Philly to square it at six apiece. Give me the home team in the tightest game on the board, and give me Jahmyr Gibbs clearing 32.
LOCK. 853.6 points, coming off a win, JSN ready to eat. Marcus can keep his history lesson, I'll take the cash.
51% is a coin with a slight thumb on it. The swing is Gibbs: 32 or more and Team Pillbert jumps to 73%, so this is a lean and nothing more.
Habibsters are on a two-game streak and have outscored Ghostu-Spider SZN by 137 points this season. Puka Nacua gives them the steadiest lever on the slate.
Zoe already beat this team by 21 in Week 1, and she's bringing a Jordan Love and Tucker Kraft stack. Rookies don't read the odds, and I'm not about to make her start now.
Two-time champ, home game, 72%? I'm backing up the truck. LOCK OF THE WEEK, and Marcus is gonna learn.
72% is the biggest edge of the week, and here's the tell: even if Puka scores under 8, Habibsters are still 56%. A 20-point Tetairoa McMillan game only gets Ghostu-Spider SZN to 45%.

picks.game: Counting or not Counting GV (Jordan) vs The fumblers (Randy)

panel.take: Four straight losses is a real trend, and I'd like to see Randy's final lineup before going further. But Derrick Henry at 26-plus makes this 88% for The fumblers.
Randy is rolling out a Caleb Williams to Colston Loveland stack, which is about as on-brand as a fantasy lineup gets. Week 1 was a 70-point beatdown, and losing streaks go to die against 1-6 teams.
I don't ride four-game losing streaks. Never have, never will. Counting or not Counting GV, LOCK, and I'll be the only one cashing it.
68% for The fumblers, and Joe Burrow needs 29-plus just to make it a coin flip for Counting or not Counting GV. Sal is fading the model on vibes; I'm not.

picks.game: No Banner only HULK (Ramon) vs Dawgs (Mekhi)

panel.take: The model has Dawgs at 54% despite the records, and Mekhi now has James Cook III and Jameson Williams from the Sonny trade. Nothing I'm hearing changes the number, so I'll lean with it.
Ramon is 6-3 all-time against Mekhi and won the Week 1 meeting by nearly 80 points. The best team in this league does not lose to a 2-5 team because a spreadsheet said so.
6-1, 927 points, three straight wins. I'm not fading that for a computer. LOCK, and Nina can explain her math to me Monday.
Yes, Dawgs are 2-5. They're also a 54% favorite, and Ja'Marr Chase at 27-plus pushes that to 75%. Records don't play this week's games; lineups do.
